verdict: Service in the focus hours is significantly worse than the baseline on lateness_sec, late_share.

evidence: [F] 100% of late trains were already late at Smith-9 Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before East Broadway: 15, at Jay St-MetroTech: 4, at York St: 3, at Bergen St: 2. Largest time loss on segment York St -> Jay St-MetroTech (median +88s vs schedule).
[F] 89% of headway gaps at the target already existed at Smith-9 Sts.

[G] 100% of late trains were already late at Smith-9 Sts (inherited delay). Origins: at or before Clinton-Washington Avs: 14, at Bergen St: 7, at Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts: 4. Largest time loss on segment Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts -> Bergen St (median +140s vs schedule).
62% of hours with problems ran fewer than 90% of scheduled trains (overall service delivered 77%): cancellations or missing trips are creating gaps.
[G] Trains that would arrive at Carroll St within 180s behind a F train lose 63s more there than others (p=0.000; 56% of trips affected); 69% of problem arrivals at the target had such a conflict.
[G] 67% of the run-time loss sits on one segment (Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts -> Bergen St, median +140s): a signal timer, speed restriction, or failure on that segment.
43% of problem arrivals occurred during planned service changes (lift 0.9x).
MTA reports 'Planned ROW Work' as 34% of delays on line(s) F, G (1.5x the system share) in the analysed months.
26% of problem arrivals happened while an MTA 'rolling_stock' alert was active for the line (problem rate 63% with an alert vs 42% without, lift 1.5x).
21% of problem arrivals happened while an MTA 'fire_smoke' alert was active for the line (problem rate 63% with an alert vs 42% without, lift 1.5x).
ETAs for problem arrivals drifted 337s on average vs 154s otherwise (2.2x): trains are being held or re-dispatched upstream.
MTA reports 'Infrastructure & Equipment' as 35% of delays on line(s) F, G (1.0x the system share) in the analysed months.
MTA reports 'Police & Medical' as 16% of delays on line(s) F, G (0.7x the system share) in the analysed months.

recommendations.action: Fill cancelled trips on F, G during 20:00-21:00: check crew availability and car assignments
recommendations.rationale: Fewer trains than scheduled are running in the problem hours.
recommendations.expected_effect: Restores scheduled headways; largest APT lever available.

recommendations.action: Review merge priority and dispatch spacing at Carroll St, where F trains run ahead of G trains bound for 4 Av-9 St
recommendations.rationale: Arrivals following a train of another route are disproportionately delayed.
recommendations.expected_effect: Fewer merge conflicts; smoother headways for both services.

recommendations.action: Inspect Hoyt-Schermerhorn Sts -> Bergen St for a speed restriction, grade-time signal or signal fault; check recent work orders
recommendations.rationale: Most of the run-time loss sits on one segment.
recommendations.expected_effect: Removing the restriction recovers the segment's excess on every trip.

recommendations.action: Check weekend / late-night planned service changes for F, G; use alternates other lines at the station
recommendations.rationale: Planned work is announced in advance.

recommendations.action: Adjust the schedule so F and G slots are offset by at least half a headway at Carroll St
recommendations.expected_effect: Structural fix that survives day-to-day variability.

recommendations.action: Review the general-order (planned work) schedule for F, G; add supplement trains or move work windows off 20:00-21:00
recommendations.rationale: Problems coincide with planned service changes.
recommendations.expected_effect: Planned changes stop degrading the analysed hours.

recommendations.action: Set a gap-filling rule: dispatch the next available train from Jamaica-179 St when a gap over 10 min forms
recommendations.rationale: A fifth of arrivals follow a large gap.
recommendations.expected_effect: Caps the longest waits, which dominate the APT metric.
